tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The BYD OTD Desk Project Plan document provides a comprehensive introduction to this car sales order-to-delivery tracking system. It covers the tech stack (NestJS, React, MySQL, Docker), UI/UX design direction, roles and permissions matrix, and development phases. Start here to understand the system's purpose: tracking car requests through an 11-stage pipeline from order placement to delivery.

tour.title: Getting Started Guide
tour.description: RUNNING.md provides operational instructions for both Docker Compose-based and local development setups, default credentials, environment variable references, and an architecture diagram. This document connects the project plan to the actual codebase by showing how to spin up the full stack with MySQL, the NestJS backend, and the React frontend.

tour.title: Backend Entry Point
tour.description: Backend main.ts bootstraps the NestJS application using Fastify as the HTTP adapter. It configures CORS, URI-based API versioning (all routes under /v1/), global validation pipes, the HttpExceptionFilter for standardized error envelopes, the ResponseTransformInterceptor for consistent API responses, and Swagger documentation. This file sets up every cross-cutting concern that shapes how the entire backend behaves.
tour.languageLesson: NestJS uses a bootstrap function with NestFactory.create() to initialize the application. Fastify is chosen over Express for better performance. URI versioning (/v1/auth/login) keeps the API evolvable without breaking existing clients.

tour.title: Backend Module Wiring
tour.description: AppModule is the root NestJS module that imports and wires all feature modules: Auth, Users, Departments, Requests, Settings, Dashboard, Reports, and Email. It also configures TypeORM with MySQL via forRoot(), making database access available across all modules. This file is the dependency injection blueprint for the entire backend -- understanding its structure reveals how the application is organized into feature boundaries.

tour.title: Data Layer: Database Entities
tour.description: The TypeORM entities define the data model that underpins every feature. CarRequest is the central entity with 11 stage timestamp columns and a lifecycle status enum. Department defines pipeline stages with ordering and slug. RequestStageTransition provides an audit trail of started/completed actions. User, Setting, SettingOption, EmailConfig, and NotificationLog complete the schema. Together these entities represent the full domain of a car order tracking system.
tour.languageLesson: TypeORM entities use decorators like @Entity(), @Column(), @ManyToOne(), and @OneToMany() to map TypeScript classes to MySQL tables. The @JoinColumn() decorator on the owning side of a relationship controls which table holds the foreign key.

tour.title: Database Schema & Seeding
tour.description: The bootstrap SQL script creates the database before TypeORM migrations run. The InitialSchema migration then creates all core tables: users, departments, settings, setting_options, car_requests, and request_stage_transitions. The seeder service populates default departments, admin users, and vehicle configuration options (brands, models, colors, accessories) so the application is functional immediately after deployment.
tour.languageLesson: TypeORM migrations use async up/down methods with QueryRunner to apply and revert schema changes. The Migration:generate CLI creates migrations from entity changes, while the bootstrap init.sql handles the one-time database creation that Docker entrypoints require.

tour.title: Authentication & Authorization
tour.description: The auth module manages JWT-based login with bcrypt password verification, a Passport JWT strategy that loads the full user profile on each request, and a RolesGuard that enforces role-based access by checking decorator metadata. The permission matrix centrally defines which roles can perform stage transitions in which departments and which pages each role can access. This layered security model gates every action in the system.

tour.title: Pipeline Core: Stage Transitions & Request Management
tour.description: Three services form the heart of the business logic. PipelineStageResolverService defines the 11-stage pipeline with conditional routing (e.g., PDI vs Accessories paths) and validates role authorization per stage. StageTransitionsService manages the transition lifecycle within database transactions, enforcing pipeline ordering (previous stage must complete before next starts). RequestsService handles CRUD, paginated search/filter queries, auto-generated request numbers, lifecycle transitions (cancel/archive/reactivate), and CSV export.
tour.languageLesson: NestJS services use @Injectable() decorators and are injected into controllers via constructor injection. Database transactions are managed with QueryRunner from TypeORM, allowing multi-step operations (stage validation + insert transition + update request) to commit or roll back atomically.

tour.title: Frontend Entry & App Shell
tour.description: The frontend starts from index.html which loads main.tsx, which mounts the React app with StrictMode. App.tsx sets up the complete application structure: React Router for client-side routing, React Query provider for server state management, and auth hydration that checks for a stored JWT token on page load. The layout components -- AppShell, ProtectedLayout, and Sidebar -- provide the authenticated app wrapper with role-based navigation filtering.
tour.languageLesson: React 19 with StrictMode double-invokes effects and reducers in development to detect side effects. React Query (@tanstack/react-query) manages server-state caching and background refetching, separate from client-side state which uses Zustand.

tour.title: Frontend Shared Types & API Client
tour.description: The types/request.ts file is the most depended-upon file in the entire codebase (fan-in of 20), defining CarRequest, Department, PipelineStage enum, and API response envelopes used by every frontend component. The API client (services/api.ts, fan-in of 15) is an Axios instance that attaches JWT tokens via request interceptor and redirects to /login on 401 responses. The auth store (Zustand) manages login/logout, token persistence in localStorage, session hydration, and role-based route resolution.
tour.languageLesson: Axios interceptors provide middleware-style request/response processing. The request interceptor attaches the JWT Bearer token from the auth store, while the response interceptor catches 401s and redirects. This keeps auth logic centralized rather than duplicated in every API call.

tour.title: Tracker: The Core Pipeline Page
tour.description: TrackerPage is the highest fan-out component (14 imports), orchestrating the entire request tracking workflow. It composes TrackerToolbar (search, filter, column visibility, CSV export), TrackerTable (pipeline columns per department stage, pagination, row selection, role-based action buttons), SelectedRequestActions (stage start/complete, lifecycle operations), BulkActionBar (multi-request transitions), and RequestFormDrawer (create/edit/delete). The useStageActions hook provides the frontend's pipeline logic hub: resolveCurrentStage determines a request's position, getAvailableAction maps role to permitted stage transitions.

tour.title: Dashboard, Reports & Settings Pages
tour.description: DashboardPage provides a high-level overview with stats cards, a month-over-month comparison bar chart, a pipeline funnel visualization, and a recent requests table. ReportsPage (admin-only) offers aggregated analytics: PDI/accessories duration averages and request counts by brand, type, model, and consultant. SettingsPage provides a complete admin panel for managing dropdown options (brands, models, variants, colors, accessories), request types, final inspection outcomes, email SMTP configuration, and user accounts.

tour.title: Containerization & Deployment
tour.description: The project uses multi-stage Docker builds for both backend and frontend. The backend Dockerfile compiles TypeScript in a builder stage and runs only production dependencies in the final stage on port 3000. The frontend Dockerfile builds the Vite/React app in one stage and serves it via nginx on port 80. Docker Compose orchestrates the full stack: development mode uses volume mounts for live reload, while production mode adds an nginx reverse proxy that routes /api/ requests to the backend.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds use multiple FROM statements in a single Dockerfile. The builder stage includes dev dependencies for compilation, while the final runtime stage copies only compiled artifacts. This keeps production images small by excluding build tooling and source files.
